citations.narrative:
An APHIS official observed an enclosure housing 1 bongo and 3 addaxes with a loose section of fencing material. This
loose fencing material exposed small metal prongs that were approximately at eye level with the bongo. Maintenance
issues such as this present an injury risk to animals. The facility must ensure outdoor housing facilities are structurally
sound and maintained in good repair to protect the animals from injury. This issue was corrected at the time of the
inspection. To remain corrected from October 19, 2026, forward.

An APHIS official observed two enclosures housing 2 domestic ducks and 5 domestic ducks, respectively, that did not
contain an adequate pool or aquatic area. Although water was provided for the animals, it was not of sufficient surface
area or depth to allow each bird to bathe, swim, or forage. Failure to provide an adequate aquatic area to wading and
aquatic birds prevents them from exhibiting species-specific behaviors. The facility must ensure that adequate pools or
aquatic areas are provided to wading and aquatic birds of sufficient surface area and depth to allow each bird to make
normal postural and social adjustments, as indicated above. This issue was corrected at the time of the inspection. To
remain corrected from October 19, 2026, forward.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
